title: Smart Machine Learning for Solving the Full Electron-Nuclear Schrödinger Equation with a Quantum-Chemically Inspired Wavefunction Ansatz
authors: Yaolong Zhang, Bin Jiang, Hua Guo
abstract: Directly solving the full electron-nuclear Schrödinger equation remains one of the grand challenges in quantum mechanics. Here, we propose a quantum-chemically motivated orbital-based neural network wavefunction ansatz with explicit many-body electron-electron correlation terms, with parameters depending on the entire electron-nuclear configuration, enabling an accurate description of strongly correlated and/or multi-reference electronic structures by a single Slater-determinant across a broad nuclear configuration space. To train this wavefunction, we further develop an efficient hybrid optimization strategy that combines the variational Monte Carlo technique with local-energy constraints, mitigating the intrinsic sampling bias of the former and considerably reducing the statistical error. These advances are embedded in a unified neural network framework, Schrödinger, enabling the determination of globally accurate potential energy surfaces with a single training for systems ranging from strongly correlated diatomic molecules, triatomic reactions containing conical intersections, to polyatomic multi-reference molecules. This work offers a practical machine-learning tool for solving the electron-nuclear Schrödinger equation and capturing full quantum effects beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
summary: The authors present SchrödingerNet, a novel machine-learning framework designed to solve the full electron-nuclear Schrödinger equation. By using a quantum-chemically inspired, configuration-adaptive wavefunction ansatz, it accurately models strongly correlated and multi-reference electronic structures. This allows for the determination of global PESs without relying on the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
main_problem: Directly solving the full electron-nuclear Schrödinger equation is computationally prohibitive due to the exponential complexity of the many-body system.
main_result: The proposed framework accurately determines globally accurate Potential Energy Surfaces (PESs) and captures full quantum effects beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation using a single training procedure.
method: A quantum-chemically motivated, orbital-based neural network wavefunction ansatz is developed and trained using a hybrid optimization strategy combining Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) with local-energy constraints.
model_or_system: The system involves molecular electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom governed by the full non-relativistic Hamiltonian. The wavefunction ansatz is a single Slater-determinant whose orbitals explicitly depend on both electronic and nuclear coordinates.
key_observables: Electronic energies, Potential Energy Surfaces (PESs), and convergence rates for various molecular systems (e.g., $	ext{H}+	ext{H}_2$, $	ext{C}_4	ext{H}_4$).
important_parameters: The explicit inclusion of electron-electron correlation (EEC) terms and the use of configuration-adaptive orbital parameters are key features.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that a single Slater-determinant, augmented with explicit EEC terms, is sufficient to describe strongly correlated and multi-reference electronic states across the nuclear configuration space.
figures_summary: Figures compare learning curves for electronic energies (with/without EEC term, varying determinants) and show PES comparisons for reactions ($	ext{H}+	ext{H}_2$) and molecular geometries ($	ext{NH}_3$).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the challenge of the full SE, proposes the SchrödingerNet framework with its specific ansatz, details the hybrid VMC/local-energy training strategy, and validates its performance across various molecular benchmarks.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, machine-learning-driven tool to tackle the full quantum dynamics of molecules, moving beyond the limitations of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation for studying non-adiabatic processes.
